title: No Touch? Non-Contact Forces Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
Kick a ball and it flies. Drop a pen and it falls with nothing touching it. Aarav rubs a plastic comb in his dry hair, and tiny bits of paper jump up to it before it even touches them. How can a pull cross a gap? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 4, Laws of Motion) we sort forces into contact forces (push, normal force, friction, tension, air drag) and non-contact forces (gravity, magnetic, electric).

On a live motion notebook a hand moves toward a block and a charged comb moves toward a paper bit, while the readout and a force vs gap graph move with them: the hand's push stays zero until the gap is zero, the comb's pull grows smoothly as the gap shrinks until it beats the paper's weight (example figures, shape only). A slow-mo replay draws the forces as the paper lifts. Then we see step by step why every force is an interaction between two bodies, why contact forces are really electric forces between atoms, two pause-and-think questions, a worked example with a magnet on a steel door, the exam trap about the force of the throw, and an original NEET pattern question.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.
